decisions.reason: As a flagship reusable harvesting crate, it fits the firm's core know-how in returnable plastic logistics packaging and gives a large German manufacturer enough learning scope to refine rather than withdraw it.

A foldable large container line with several models is highly related to the firm's existing engineering, customer base and manufacturing capabilities, so absorptive capacity argues for continued commercialization.
A stackable plastic crate is close to the firm's established packaging competence and should be easy to improve through customer feedback even if it was not heavily highlighted online.
The medium-duty rackable pallet sits within the firm's pallet and reusable transport portfolio, though some overlap and competitive pressure make it a bit more vulnerable than the strongest launches.

The spill-retention pallet is more niche and was quickly de-emphasized on the website, suggesting weaker traction in an area somewhat less central to the firm's main reusable logistics packaging knowledge base.
The plastic pallet with load retainers is related to the firm's pallet expertise but its reduced prominence suggests limited distinct market pull, making resource reallocation the more likely choice.
